name: Battle of Ayacucho

phases.title: The armies face each other
phases.text: The independentist line formed an angle, with Córdova on the right, La Mar on the left, Miller's cavalry in the centre and Lara in reserve. The royalists stood on the heights of Condorcunca, with Valdés' vanguard on their right.

phases.title: The royalists come down the slope
phases.text: Canterac's plan sent Valdés across the Pampas to turn Sucre's left while the rest of the army descended frontally from the hill. The royalists moved onto an exposed slope, and Córdova's division, supported by Miller's cavalry, fired on them.

phases.title: Villalobos is pushed back and Monet is surrounded
phases.text: Córdova's fire pushed back Villalobos' scattered men. Monet crossed the ravine without waiting for his cavalry, formed two battalions and was surrounded by the independentist division before the rest of his troops could form.

phases.title: Monet's division breaks and Ferraz charges
phases.text: Monet was wounded and his scattered divisions dragged the militia with them. Ferraz's cavalry charged the squadrons pursuing Monet's broken left, but crossfire from the infantry caused heavy casualties.

phases.title: Valdés attacks the isolated building
phases.text: On the other flank, La Mar and Lara stopped the assault of Valdés' veterans, who had gone forward to take the isolated building. The independentists were reinforced and attacked again, helped by Córdova's division.

phases.title: The reserve scatters and the viceroy is taken
phases.text: Canterac led the reserve across the plain, but its recruits scattered before they met the enemy. By one o'clock the viceroy had been wounded and made prisoner. Valdés retreated to the hill held by his rearguard.

note: The accounts give the order of battle and the movements but no map. The river Pampas is placed on the left of Sucre's line, the ravine between the two armies and the isolated building in front of the independentist left; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. Miller's account of the army's layout differs from Sucre's report on the Junín Hussars (Sucre puts them under La Mar, Miller in his own cavalry); the plan follows Sucre's report. The royalist order of battle is not given by wing, so the places of Monet, Villalobos and Ferraz are judgement.
